narrative:
The model estimates an 82% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of professional experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and the fact that you have received other job offers while working here. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), the model sees mid-level experience like yours as often signaling readiness to move on to new opportunities. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in your current organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction. This tenure is actually the most common range among those expected to stay, yet in combination with your broader experience it signals a natural point where people tend to seek change.

Finally, having received other job opportunities during your time here was a significant factor pulling the prediction toward departure. Most employees the model expects to stay (77%) do not receive such external offers.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional responsibilities, better recognition, or improved compensation could increase your sense of stability and satisfaction. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding before making any decisions. (248 words)
